gap.description: Every top result is either a bare encyclopedic overview (Wikipedia, thin sourcing, no camp grounding) or a generic gym/brand blog post with zero connection to a real, currently operating Chiang Mai camp. None combine deep, accurate ritual explanation with an actual first-person account of the Wai Kru performed at a specific, named camp — and none give a visiting foreigner practical, respectful guidance on what to do or feel the first time they see or perform it. YouTube dominates the visual side of this query but with no accompanying deep-dive text, leaving a real opening for a text-first, video-friendly explainer written from inside an operating camp.

weakness: Wikipedia's historical claims are under-sourced (multiple citation-needed tags) and entirely omits regional style variation (Korat, Chaiya, Lopburi)
Evolve MMA covers regional variation well but is disconnected from Chiang Mai and reads as generic gym content with a newsletter CTA bolt-on
YOKKAO's piece leans promotional (video from their own training center) rather than genuinely explanatory, with no author or sourcing
none of the top 5 results offer a family/beginner-friendly framing — all are written for a hardcore fight-culture audience, not for a curious traveler or student
recommended_angle: Explain the Wai Kru Ram Muay with real cultural depth and respect (etymology, the two parts, regional style variation, what the movements symbolize) but anchor it in Wildcat's actual Chiang Mai camp and family — what visitors and students see and feel when it's performed there, written warmly for curious travelers and beginners rather than hardcore fight fans, positioning Wildcat as a place where this tradition is lived daily, not just described.
